newsitem.title: CHINA: China's dam funding seen short 30.8 bln yuan.
newsitem.headline: China's dam funding seen short 30.8 bln yuan.

text.p: The capital shortfall of China's Three Gorges dam project is expected to reach about 30.8 billion yuan ($3.7 billion) by the year 2005, the Economic Daily said on Friday.
The total cost of the huge water control project, due to be completed in the year 2009, was expected to hit 203.9 billion yuan, the newspaper said.

The Three Gorges Project Foundation and revenue allocated from the downstream Gezhouba dam, currently China's biggest hydropower plant, would jointly contribute 100 billion yuan to the project, it said.
The State Development Bank would provide a total of 30 billion yuan in loans in the 1994-2003 period, it said.
The dam would start generating power in the year 2003 and was likely to generate a total of 67 billion yuan income by the year 2009, it said. Part of the income would be reinvested.
State policy loans, commercial bank loans and bond issues would fill the financial gaps, it said.
Project managers were also considering future listing of the Gezhouba power station and the Three Gorges dam itself, it said, but gave no further details.
